l: The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: After the death of Moses, the LORD commands Joshua, son of Nun, to lead all the people across the Jordan into the land promised to the children of Israel, whose borders stretch from the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates and the great sea. The LORD promises that no one will stand against Joshua and that he will be with him as he was with Moses, and urges him repeatedly to be strong and courageous and to keep and meditate on the law of Moses. Joshua then orders the officers to tell the people to prepare food, since they will cross the Jordan within three days. He reminds the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh of Moses' command that their fighting men must cross armed ahead of their brothers until all have received rest. They pledge to obey Joshua as they obeyed Moses, and declare that anyone who rebels against his commands will be put to death.

l: Joshua, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: Joshua, son of Nun and Moses' servant, is commissioned by the LORD to lead the people across the Jordan and is told to be strong, courageous, and faithful to the law. He commands the officers to have the people prepare to cross within three days and reminds the eastern tribes of their duty to help their brothers. The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh pledge to obey him as they did Moses.

l: LORD, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The LORD speaks to Joshua after Moses' death, telling him to cross the Jordan and promising him the land, victory over all opponents, and his presence as with Moses. He promises not to fail or forsake Joshua and commands him to be strong and courageous. He is also named as the one who gives rest and land to the tribes.

l: Moses, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: Moses is described as the LORD's servant who is now dead. The LORD says he will be with Joshua as he was with Moses, and Moses' law and his earlier command about land beyond the Jordan are invoked. The eastern tribes promise to listen to Joshua just as they listened to Moses.

l: Jordan, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The Jordan is the river that Joshua and all the people are told to cross into the land. Within three days the people are to pass over it. Moses had given the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.

l: promised land (land given to Israel), The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The LORD declares he is giving this land to the children of Israel, as he swore to their fathers. Its border is described as running from the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates, including all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea in the west. Joshua is given every place the sole of his foot will tread.

l: children of Israel, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The children of Israel are the people to whom the LORD is giving the land, and Joshua is to cause them to inherit it. They are told through the officers to prepare food for crossing the Jordan within three days.

l: Reubenites, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The Reubenites are addressed by Joshua and reminded of Moses' command that their wives, little ones, and livestock stay in the land east of the Jordan while their armed fighting men cross ahead of their brothers. They join in answering that they will do all Joshua commands and go wherever he sends them.

l: Gadites, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The Gadites are addressed by Joshua with the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh and reminded that their mighty men must cross armed to help their brothers until the land is possessed. They answer with a pledge to obey Joshua in everything.

l: half-tribe of Manasseh, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The half-tribe of Manasseh is addressed by Joshua together with the Reubenites and Gadites. Its fighting men are to cross the Jordan armed to help their brothers before returning to their possession east of the Jordan. They join in promising to obey Joshua.

l: book of the law of Moses, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The LORD tells Joshua that the book of the law must not depart from his mouth and that he is to meditate on it day and night. He is to observe all that is written in it and not turn from it right or left, so that he will prosper and have good success.

l: crossing of the Jordan, The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua / Chapter 1
s: The LORD commands Joshua to arise and cross the Jordan with all the people into the land. Joshua has the officers tell the people to prepare food because they will cross within three days. The armed men of the eastern tribes are to cross ahead of their brothers.

l: The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Joshua the son of Nun secretly sends two spies from Shittim to view the land, including Jericho, and they lodge at the house of a prostitute named Rahab. When the king of Jericho demands that she hand them over, Rahab hides them under flax stalks on her roof and sends the pursuers off toward the fords of the Jordan. She tells the spies that Jericho's people are terrified because of the LORD's deeds at the Red Sea and against Sihon and Og, and she asks them to swear to spare her father's house. The spies pledge their lives for hers on condition of her silence, and tell her to tie a scarlet thread in her window and gather her family in the house. She lowers them by a cord from her window in the wall and tells them to hide in the mountain for three days; they then return to Joshua and report that the LORD has delivered the land into their hands.

l: Rahab, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Rahab, a prostitute in Jericho, takes in the two spies, hides them under flax on her roof, and misleads the king's messengers by saying they had already left. She declares her belief that the LORD has given Israel the land, asks the spies to swear to spare her family, lowers them by a cord from her window, and ties the scarlet line in the window as agreed.

l: Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Joshua the son of Nun secretly sends two men from Shittim to view the land, including Jericho. At the end of the unit the spies return to him and tell him all that happened, saying that the LORD has delivered the land into their hands.

l: two spies (sent by Joshua), The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: The two spies enter Jericho, lodge at Rahab's house, and are hidden by her from the king's pursuers. They swear to deal kindly and truly with her, set the scarlet thread and house-gathering conditions, and then hide in the mountain for three days before returning to Joshua with the report that the inhabitants melt away before them.

l: king of Jericho, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: The king of Jericho is told that Israelite men have come to spy out the land and sends to Rahab demanding that she bring them out. He is deceived by her, and his pursuers chase the spies toward the fords of the Jordan without finding them.

l: Jericho, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Jericho is the city the spies are sent to view, and its gate is shut at dark. Rahab reports that its inhabitants' hearts have melted in fear of Israel, and the spies later report that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before them.

l: LORD, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: The LORD is described by Rahab as having given Israel the land, having dried up the water of the Red Sea, and being God in heaven above and on earth beneath. The spies take the oath in his name and, on returning, say that he has delivered all the land into their hands.

l: Rahab's family (Rahab's father's house), The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Rahab asks that her father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all they have be saved alive from death. The spies agree to protect those who are with her in the house, and instruct her to gather her father, mother, brothers, and all her father's household inside; whoever goes out into the street will bear their own blood.

l: scarlet thread (Rahab's window sign), The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: The spies tell Rahab to tie a line of scarlet thread in the window she used to let them down, as the sign for when they come into the land. She ties the scarlet line in the window after sending them away.

l: oath (Rahab and the spies' oath), The Book of Joshua, Chapter 2
s: Rahab asks the spies to swear by the LORD to deal kindly with her father's house, and they agree, pledging their lives for hers if she does not talk about their business. They declare themselves guiltless of the oath if she speaks of it, or if anyone leaves her house, and she accepts the terms.

l: The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: Joshua leads the children of Israel from Shittim to the Jordan, where they camp for three days before crossing. The officers instruct the people to follow the ark of the covenant carried by the Levitical priests, keeping about two thousand cubits behind it. Joshua tells the people to sanctify themselves, and the LORD promises to magnify Joshua so Israel will know he is with him as he was with Moses. Joshua announces that the ark will cause the Jordan's waters to be cut off and that the living God will drive out the Canaanite, Hittite, Hivite, Perizzite, Girgashite, Amorite, and Jebusite. When the priests' feet touch the water, the river stops and piles up in one heap at Adam, and all Israel crosses on dry ground near Jericho while the priests stand firm in the middle of the Jordan.

l: Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: Joshua rises early, moves the people from Shittim to the Jordan, and tells them to sanctify themselves because the LORD will do wonders. He commands the priests to take up the ark and cross over before the people, and announces that the Jordan will be cut off and the nations driven out. The LORD tells him that he will be magnified in the sight of all Israel as Moses was.

l: children of Israel, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The children of Israel camp at the Jordan, are told to follow the ark at a distance of about two thousand cubits, and are told to sanctify themselves. They then pass over the Jordan on dry ground near Jericho until the whole nation has crossed.

l: Jordan, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The Jordan is overflowing all its banks, as it does all the time of harvest. When the priests' feet dip into its edge, its waters coming down from above stand in one heap a great way off at Adam, near Zarethan, and the waters toward the Salt Sea are wholly cut off, leaving dry ground for the crossing.

l: ark of the covenant, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The ark of the covenant is carried by the priests ahead of the people, and the people are to follow it to learn the way. It is called the ark of the Lord of all the earth, and its passing into the Jordan is the sign that cuts off the waters. It rests in the middle of the Jordan on dry ground until all the nation has crossed.

l: Levitical priests, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The Levitical priests bear the ark and go before the people at Joshua's command. They are told to stand still in the Jordan at the brink of the waters, and when their feet dip in, the waters are cut off. They stand firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan until all Israel has crossed.

l: LORD, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The LORD tells Joshua that he will begin to magnify him in the sight of all Israel, so they know he is with Joshua as he was with Moses. He instructs the priests to stand still in the Jordan, and through the ark he cuts off the river's waters. Joshua declares that this shows the living God is among Israel and will drive out the seven named nations before them.

l: crossing of the Jordan, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 3
s: The crossing takes place after three days of camping, with the priests bearing the ark going first into the overflowing Jordan. The waters stop and rise in one heap at Adam, and the people pass over near Jericho on dry ground. The priests stand firm in the riverbed until the whole nation has passed completely over.

l: The Book of Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: After all the nation had crossed the Jordan, the LORD told Joshua to have twelve men, one from each tribe, take twelve stones from the middle of the river where the priests' feet stood firm and carry them to the camp as a memorial. Joshua carried this out and also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, while the priests bearing the ark stood there until everything was finished and the people hurried across. The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh crossed armed before Israel, about forty thousand men, and the LORD magnified Joshua so that the people feared him as they had feared Moses. At the LORD's command the priests came up out of the Jordan, the waters returned to their place and overflowed their banks, and the people camped at Gilgal on the tenth day of the first month, where Joshua set up the stones and explained that they testify to the LORD's mighty hand and should lead all to fear him.

l: Joshua, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: Joshua relays the LORD's instructions to the twelve chosen men, sets up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, and later sets up the twelve stones at Gilgal. The LORD magnifies him in the sight of all Israel, so that they fear him as they feared Moses all his life. He tells the people how to explain the stones to their children.

l: LORD, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: The LORD commands Joshua to have twelve men take twelve stones from the Jordan, and later commands that the priests come up out of the river. He magnifies Joshua before all Israel. The stones are explained as a testimony that his hand is mighty, that he dried up the Jordan as he did the Red Sea, and that he is to be feared forever.

l: Jordan, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: The Jordan's waters stayed cut off before the ark while the priests stood in its middle and the people crossed on dry land. Twelve stones were taken from its middle and twelve others were set up where the priests stood. When the priests came up, its waters returned to their place and went over all its banks as before.

l: twelve stones, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: Twelve men, one from each tribe, took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan and carried them to the camp as a memorial for Israel forever, to answer the questions of future children. Joshua set them up at Gilgal. Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, where they remain to this day.

l: children of Israel, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: Israel completed the crossing of the Jordan, hurrying over while the priests stood in the river. Forty thousand armed men from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh passed over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho. The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and encamped at Gilgal, and they feared Joshua as they had feared Moses.

l: ark of the covenant, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: The ark was borne by priests who stood in the middle of the Jordan until the people had crossed. After all the people were over, it crossed with the priests in their presence. The waters of the Jordan were cut off before it, which is the reason given for the memorial stones.

l: Levitical priests, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: The priests who bore the ark stood firm in the middle of the Jordan until everything the LORD commanded was finished and the people had crossed. At Joshua's command, relaying the LORD's, they came up out of the river. When their feet touched dry ground, the waters returned to their place.

l: Gilgal, The Book of Joshua, Chapter 4
s: Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho, is where Israel encamped after coming up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month. Joshua set up there the twelve stones taken from the river. It is the place where the stones serve as a memorial for future generations.
